title: Queues & Deques
subtitle: A queue preserves arrival order; a deque also keeps only the live candidates needed at either boundary.
variables: n = input items, k = window size or capacity, V/E = all supplied graph vertices/edges (including neighbor-only vertices and edges scanned during validation), R/C = grid rows/columns, w = maximum BFS frontier width, q = current queue size. Bounds assume O(1) reference operations and fixed-size numeric comparisons/arithmetic; Python large integers cost by bit length. Hash-based graph bounds are expected and include O(key length) hashing/comparison for long keys. Auxiliary space excludes returned output unless stated; deque storage itself is counted. Inputs are finite; graphs use hashable vertices. Single-threaded algorithms are not producer/consumer synchronization.
